entries.name: GPIO_read
entries.description: Reads the digital input value (HIGH or LOW) from a specified GPIO pin using digitalRead().

sections.description:
port: The GPIO pin number connected to the digital input device.
INPUT_PULLUP: Configures the pin as an input with an internal pull-up resistor.
Returns HIGH (1) if the pin is HIGH and LOW (0) if the pin is LOW.

entries.name: digitalOutput
entries.description: Controls external components such as LEDs, Laser, or other devices using a digital output signal. The pin can be set HIGH to turn the component ON or LOW to turn it OFF.

sections.description:
In the setup() function configure the port as output:
pinMode(port, OUTPUT);

In the loop() function control the device state:
digitalWrite(port, HIGH);  // Turn device ON
digitalWrite(port, LOW);   // Turn device OFF

port: The external GPIO port where the device is connected. Use the port number according to the hardware documentation.

OUTPUT: Configures the selected port as an output pin.

HIGH: Sets the port voltage HIGH and turns the connected device ON.

LOW: Sets the port voltage LOW and turns the connected device OFF.
These functions do not return any value. They only control the digital state of the selected port.

entries.name: ADC_read
entries.description: Reads the analog input value from a specified GPIO pin using analogRead().

sections.description:
value = analogRead(pin);
Serial.println(value);

pin: The analog input port number.

Example analog input ports from the board:
A1 : 1
A2 : 2
Returns an integer representing the analog input value.

entries.name: pwmOutput
entries.description: Controls external components using PWM signals on a specific pin using analogWrite().

sections.description: analogWrite(pin, value);

pin: The PWM output port number.
value: Integer (0–255) representing the PWM duty cycle.

Example PWM output ports from the board:
A1 : 1
A2 : 2
No return value. The function sets the PWM duty cycle on the specified pin.

entries.name: readTouch
entries.description: Reads the capacitive touch values from the built-in touch pads on the board. The touch pads are already connected to fixed pins, so no external wiring is required.

sections.description:
Read the capacitive value from a touch pad using:

value = touchRead(port);

port : The GPIO port connected to the touch pad.

Example ports on this board:
	10, 11, 12, 13
Returns an integer value representing the raw capacitive reading of the touch pad. Lower values generally indicate that the pad is being touched.

entries.name: rgbLEDEye
entries.description: Controls the 12 built-in RGB eye LEDs using the NeoPixel LED driver. Each LED can be set to a specific RGB color value.

sections.description:
1.    Library Name: Adafruit_NeoPixel

2.    Include Syntax: #include <Adafruit_NeoPixel.h>

3.    Initialization Syntax:
	Adafruit_NeoPixel strip(NUM_LEDS, LED_PIN, NEO_GRB + NEO_KHZ800);

4.   Parameters:
	NUM_LEDS: Total number of RGB LEDs.
	LED_PIN: GPIO pin connected to the RGB LED data line.
	NEO_GRB: Color order used by the LEDs.
	NEO_KHZ800: Communication speed of the NeoPixel LEDs.

strip.setPixelColor(led_number, strip.Color(red, green, blue));
strip.show();

led_number: Index of the RGB LED to control.
red: Red color intensity (0–255).
green: Green color intensity (0–255).
blue: Blue color intensity (0–255).

Example eye LED ports:
Eye1 : 12
Eye2 : 13
Eye3 : 14
Eye4 : 15
Eye5 : 16
Eye6 : 17
Eye7 : 18
Eye8 : 19
Eye9 : 20
Eye10 : 21
Eye11 : 22
Eye12 : 23
No return value. The function updates the color of the selected RGB eye LED.

entries.name: smileLED
entries.description: Controls the four onboard Smile LEDs available on the board. Each LED is connected to a specific port and can be turned ON or OFF individually. The LEDs are arranged from left to right on ports 37, 41, 21, and 35.

sections.description:
In the setup() function, configure the Smile LED port as an output using:
pinMode(port, OUTPUT);

In the loop() function, control the LED using:
digitalWrite(port, HIGH);  // Turn the LED ON
digitalWrite(port, LOW);   // Turn the LED OFF

port: The GPIO port number where the Smile LED is connected. The Smile LEDs are connected to ports 37, 41, 21, and 35 (from left to right).

OUTPUT: Configures the selected port as an output pin.

HIGH: Turns the LED ON.

LOW: Turns the LED OFF.
No return value. The methods turn the specified Smile LED ON or OFF.

entries.name: buzzerTone
entries.description: Controls a buzzer connected to the board using a digital output pin. The buzzer produces sound by generating a square wave signal at a specific frequency.

sections.description:
Define the buzzer port and tone configuration before starting the program:

#define BUZZER_PIN 45
#define BEEP_FREQUENCY 2000
#define BEEP_DURATION 200
#define INTERVAL 2000

BUZZER_PIN: The GPIO port where the buzzer is connected. Use the correct port number according to the hardware documentation.

BEEP_FREQUENCY: The tone frequency in Hertz (Hz).

BEEP_DURATION: Duration of the beep sound in milliseconds.

INTERVAL: Delay between two beep cycles in milliseconds.

BUZZER_PIN: The GPIO port connected to the buzzer.

BEEP_FREQUENCY: The sound frequency in Hertz.

BEEP_DURATION: Time the buzzer will play the tone.

INTERVAL: Time delay between repeated beeps.
These functions do not return any value. They only generate a sound signal through the buzzer.

entries.name: externalRGB
entries.description: Controls external NeoPixel RGB LEDs connected to the board using the Adafruit NeoPixel library. Each LED's color can be controlled individually by setting red, green, and blue values.

sections.description:
Define the port and number of LEDs before creating the NeoPixel object:

#define LED_PIN 1
#define NUM_LEDS 1

LED_PIN: The GPIO port where the NeoPixel data pin is connected. Use the external port number according to the hardware documentation.
NUM_LEDS: Total number of NeoPixel LEDs connected to the port.

This example uses the Adafruit NeoPixel library to control RGB LEDs.

1.    Library Name: Adafruit_NeoPixel

2.   Include the library at the beginning of the program:
#include <Adafruit_NeoPixel.h>

3.  Library Initialization Syntax:
Adafruit_NeoPixel strip(number_of_leds, port, NEO_GRB + NEO_KHZ800);

4.  Parameters:
number_of_leds: Total number of NeoPixel LEDs connected.
port: The GPIO pin where the NeoPixel data line is connected.
NEO_GRB + NEO_KHZ800: Specifies the LED color order and communication speed used by most NeoPixel LEDs.

index: The LED number to control (0 to number_of_leds - 1).

R, G, B: Integer values (0–255) representing red, green, and blue color intensity.

strip.show(): Updates the LED strip and applies the color changes.
These functions do not return any value. They only update the color of the connected NeoPixel LEDs.

entries.name: oledDisplay
entries.description: Controls an external OLED display connected to the board using the I2C interface. You can display text at specific coordinates on the screen.

sections.description:
This example uses the Adafruit GFX and Adafruit SSD1306 libraries to control the OLED display.

1.  Library Names:
	Wire
	Adafruit_GFX
	Adafruit_SSD1306

2.   Include the libraries at the beginning of the program:
	#include <Wire.h>
	#include <Adafruit_GFX.h>
	#include <Adafruit_SSD1306.h>

3.  sLibrary Initialization Syntax:
	Adafruit_SSD1306 display(width, height, &Wire, reset_pin);

4.  Parameters:
	width  : OLED display width in pixels (usually 128).
	height : OLED display height in pixels (usually 64).
	&Wire  : I2C communication interface.
	reset_pin : Reset pin of the display (use -1 if not connected).

Define display configuration and I2C communication pins before starting the program.

#define SCREEN_WIDTH 128
#define SCREEN_HEIGHT 64
#define OLED_RESET -1
#define SCREEN_ADDRESS 0x3C
#define SDA_PIN 9
#define SCL_PIN 8

SCREEN_WIDTH and SCREEN_HEIGHT define the display resolution.
SCREEN_ADDRESS is the I2C address of the OLED display.
SDA_PIN and SCL_PIN define the I2C communication pins used to connect the display.

size : Text size multiplier.

x : X coordinate of the text position (0–127).

y : Y coordinate of the text position (0–63).

text : The message string to display on the OLED screen.

SCREEN_ADDRESS : I2C address used to communicate with the display.
These functions do not return any value. They update the OLED display with the specified text or graphics.

entries.name: servoOutput
entries.description: Controls an external servo motor connected to the board using PWM signals. The servo motor rotates to a specific angle between 0° and 180° by generating the appropriate PWM signal on the connected port.

sections.description:
This example uses the ESP32Servo library to control a servo motor.

1.  Library Name:
	ESP32Servo

2.   Include the library at the beginning of the program:
	#include <ESP32Servo.h>

3.   Library Initialization Syntax:
	Servo servoObject;

4.  Attach the servo to a pin:
	servoObject.attach(port, min_pulse, max_pulse);

5.   Parameters:
	port : The GPIO port where the servo signal wire is connected.
	min_pulse : Minimum pulse width in microseconds (typically around 500).
	max_pulse : Maximum pulse width in microseconds (typically around 2400).

Define the servo port before starting the program:

#define SERVO_PIN 1

SERVO_PIN: The GPIO port where the servo motor control wire is connected. Use the correct external port number according to the hardware documentation.

angle : The position to rotate the servo motor, specified in degrees (0–180).

SERVO_PIN : The GPIO port connected to the servo signal wire.
These functions do not return any value. They generate a PWM signal that moves the connected servo motor to the specified angle.

entries.name: pinStatus
entries.description: Holds the current status of a digital pin.

sections.description: int
0 (LOW) or 1 (HIGH)
